newsitem.title: INDONESIA: E. Timorese men break into Jakarta's French embassy.
newsitem.headline: E. Timorese men break into Jakarta's French embassy.

text.p: Three East Timorese men broke into the French embassy in Jakarta early on Tuesday morning, apparently to seek political asylum, witnesses said.

They said the three scaled the fence surrounding the French embassy compound and could be seen near the entrance porch waving a banner saying "Free East Timor". One French official could be seen talking to them but would not comment when asked if the three had sought asylum.

It was the latest in a series of break-ins at foreign missions in Jakarta by Timorese seeking to flee their troubled homeland. At least 93 East Timorese have been granted asylum in Portugal since September last year after breaking into Jakarta embassies.

Indonesia invaded East Timor, a former Portuguese colony, in 1975 and annexed it a year later in an act not recognised by the United Nations. Many East Timorese oppose Jakarta's rule and accuse Indonesian troops in the territory of human rights abuses.
The French embassy in Jakarta has been particularly vulnerable to the break-ins, with at least five reported since last year.

But three East Timorese who were seen within the mission compound after a break-in in October later said their demand for asylum was rejected and they were thrown out of the premises. French embassy officials said no East Timorese had entered the mission.
